summary.en: A student receives a $5,000 scholarship email that asks for a fee and personal data. Is it real?
summary.vi: Một sinh viên nhận email báo trúng học bổng 5.000 USD nhưng bị yêu cầu nộp phí và cung cấp thông tin cá nhân. Thật hay giả?

briefing.en: Emma Tran, a second-year student, has received an email saying she has won the International Excellence Scholarship worth $5,000. The email asks her to pay a processing fee and send personal information within 48 hours. Emma is not sure the email is real and has asked the English Detective Agency for help. Read the documents, interview the people involved and decide what is really happening. Then write a report with your conclusion and recommendations.
briefing.vi: Emma Tran, sinh viên năm hai, nhận được email báo đã giành học bổng International Excellence trị giá 5.000 USD. Email yêu cầu cô nộp phí xử lý hồ sơ và gửi thông tin cá nhân trong 48 giờ. Emma không chắc email này là thật nên nhờ English Detective Agency giúp đỡ. Hãy đọc tài liệu, phỏng vấn những người liên quan và xác định điều gì đang thực sự xảy ra. Sau đó viết báo cáo nêu kết luận và khuyến nghị.

objectives.en: Compare the scholarship email with the official university documents.

documents.title: Congratulations! You have won a $5,000 International Scholarship

meta.Subject: Congratulations! You have won a $5,000 International Scholarship

documents.body:
Dear Emma Tran,

Congratulations! We are happy to inform you that you have been selected for the International Excellence Scholarship worth $5,000.

To receive your scholarship, you must pay a processing fee of $150 within 48 hours. Please send the payment by bank transfer to the account below and reply with a copy of your passport and your bank card number.

Bank: Global Trust Bank
Account name: IU Scholarship Services
Account number: 7782 0091 4456

If we do not receive your payment within 48 hours, the scholarship will be given to another student.

The university logo and our signature confirm that this message is official.

Best regards,
Mr. David Miller
International Scholarship Office
Contact: awards@intl-univ-scholarships.com

glossary.definition: money you pay so that an organisation will deal with your application
sending money from one bank account to another

documents.title: Official Announcement: International Excellence Scholarship 2027
documents.body:
INTERNATIONAL UNIVERSITY – SCHOLARSHIP OFFICE

The International Excellence Scholarship provides $5,000 to ten undergraduate students for the 2027–2028 academic year.

Application period: 1 February – 28 February 2027.

Results: Successful students will be informed through the Student Portal on 20 March 2027. Results are not sent by private email.

Important: The university never asks students to pay any fee to apply for or receive a scholarship. All official emails come from addresses ending in @iu.edu.

Questions? Visit Room 204, Building A, or email scholarships@iu.edu.

Mr. David Miller
Head of the Scholarship Office

glossary.definition: a university student who is studying for a first degree
glossary.vi: sinh viên đại học (hệ cử nhân)

glossary.definition: the university website where students log in to see their information

documents.title: RE: Congratulations! You have won a $5,000 International Scholarship
documents.body:
From: Emma Tran <emma.tran@student.iu.edu> – 18:20

Hello, thank you for your email. I applied for the scholarship in February. Can I pay the fee after I receive the money? Also, why do you need my bank card number?

From: International Scholarship Office <awards@intl-univ-scholarships.com> – 18:45

Dear Emma, the fee must be paid first. This is the normal process for all international scholarships. We need your card number to send the money quickly. Please do not tell other students about this award because the list is confidential. You have 46 hours left.

glossary.definition: secret; not to be shared with other people

documents.title: Student IT Help – Staying safe online
documents.body:
Phishing emails try to steal your money or personal information. Be careful if an email:

- comes from an address that does not end in @iu.edu,
- asks you to pay money or send your bank details,
- says you must act within a very short time,
- asks you to keep the message secret.

If you receive a suspicious email, do not reply. Forward it to security@iu.edu and delete it.

The IT Help Desk is open Monday to Friday, 8:00–17:00, in the library.

glossary.definition: a trick in which criminals send messages that look real to steal money or information
making you feel that something is wrong or dishonest

documents.title: Scholarship Application Guidelines 2027

meta.Source: Student Portal → Scholarships → How to apply

documents.body:
1. Complete the online form on the Student Portal before 28 February.

2. Upload your transcript and one recommendation letter.

3. The Scholarship Committee meets on 15 March to choose the winners.

4. Winners must sign the scholarship agreement in Room 204 with their student ID card.

5. The money is paid directly into the student's tuition account in September.

glossary.definition: an official list of a student's courses and marks
the student's account used to pay university fees

documents.title: Email Security Check – Ticket #4471
documents.body:
Summary of the check:

The message was sent from a server outside the university network. The domain intl-univ-scholarships.com was registered on 1 March 2027, two days before the email was sent. The bank account in the message does not belong to International University.

Recommendation: Do not pay. Block the sender and report the message to the Scholarship Office.

questions.prompt: Which details in the scholarship email are inconsistent with the official announcement? Give two examples in 1–3 sentences.
keyPoints: The email asks for a processing fee, but the university never asks students to pay a fee.
The sender's address does not end in @iu.edu.

questions.sampleAnswer: The email asks Emma to pay a $150 fee, but the official announcement says the university never asks students to pay any fee. Also, the email comes from an address that does not end in @iu.edu, and results are only published on the Student Portal on 20 March.

evidence.excerpt: you must pay a processing fee of $150 within 48 hours
evidence.label: Email demands a $150 fee within 48 hours
evidence.explanation: The email clearly requests a payment and creates time pressure – a typical sign of a scam.

evidence.excerpt: reply with a copy of your passport and your bank card number
evidence.label: Email asks for passport and bank card number
evidence.explanation: Asking for passport and card details is a phishing sign; the real process never needs a bank card.

evidence.label: Sender address is not an @iu.edu address
evidence.explanation: The sender uses an outside domain, while official emails always end in @iu.edu.

evidence.excerpt: The university logo and our signature confirm that this message is official
evidence.label: Sender claims the logo proves the email is official
evidence.explanation: Logos and signatures can be copied easily; the claim is not proof.

evidence.label: The scholarship is worth $5,000
evidence.explanation: The amount matches the real scholarship, so it does not help decide whether the email is genuine (scammers copy real details).

evidence.excerpt: The university never asks students to pay any fee to apply for or receive a scholarship
evidence.label: Official policy: no fees for scholarships
evidence.explanation: Directly contradicts the fee request in the email.

evidence.excerpt: All official emails come from addresses ending in @iu.edu
evidence.label: Official emails end in @iu.edu
evidence.explanation: Shows that the sender's address is not an official university address.

evidence.excerpt: Successful students will be informed through the Student Portal on 20 March 2027
evidence.label: Results come via the Student Portal on 20 March
evidence.explanation: The email arrived on 3 March, before results exist, and by private email instead of the portal.

evidence.label: Ten students receive the scholarship
evidence.explanation: The number of winners does not show whether this email is genuine.

evidence.excerpt: I applied for the scholarship in February
evidence.label: Emma says she applied in February
evidence.explanation: Emma's own statement; it can be confirmed by the Scholarship Office but does not prove the email is real.

evidence.excerpt: This is the normal process for all international scholarships
evidence.label: Sender claims paying first is normal
evidence.explanation: An unsupported claim by the sender, contradicted by the official policy.

evidence.excerpt: Please do not tell other students about this award because the list is confidential
evidence.label: Sender asks Emma to keep it secret
evidence.explanation: Requests for secrecy are a listed sign of phishing.

evidence.excerpt: says you must act within a very short time
evidence.label: IT warning: short deadlines are a phishing sign
evidence.explanation: Matches the 48-hour deadline in the email.

evidence.excerpt: The IT Help Desk is open Monday to Friday
evidence.label: IT Help Desk opening days
evidence.explanation: Opening hours are not relevant to whether the email is genuine.

evidence.excerpt: The Scholarship Committee meets on 15 March to choose the winners
evidence.label: Winners are chosen on 15 March
evidence.explanation: On 3 March no winners had been chosen yet.

evidence.excerpt: The money is paid directly into the student's tuition account in September
evidence.label: Money goes to the tuition account in September
evidence.explanation: The real process never needs a bank card number.

evidence.excerpt: The domain intl-univ-scholarships.com was registered on 1 March 2027, two days before the email was sent
evidence.label: Sender domain created two days before the email
evidence.explanation: A newly created outside domain strongly indicates a fake sender.

evidence.excerpt: The bank account in the message does not belong to International University
evidence.label: Bank account is not the university's
evidence.explanation: The payment would go to someone else, not the university.

conclusion.question: What is the most reasonable conclusion about the scholarship email?

options.text: The email is a phishing scam that pretends to come from the Scholarship Office.
The email is genuine, and Emma should pay the fee quickly to keep the scholarship.
The email is genuine but was sent early by mistake.
The email was sent by the university's partner bank.

Other students have already paid the fee (no document shows this).
Emma's university account has been hacked (there is no evidence of this).

writingTask.prompt: Write an investigation report to the Head of Student Affairs about the scholarship email Emma received. Include: a summary of the case, the evidence you collected, your analysis, your conclusion and your recommendations.
writingTask.audience: Head of Student Affairs, International University
keyPoints: States that the email is a phishing scam / not from the university.
Uses the contradiction between the fee request and the official no-fee policy.
Uses the sender's non-@iu.edu address (and/or the newly registered domain).
Notes that the email came before the official results date and not through the Student Portal.
Recommends not paying or sharing data, reporting to security@iu.edu and warning other students.

documents: Start with the scholarship email and the official announcement.
Compare how and when the university really announces results.
Look for money, dates and email addresses that do not match.
evidence: Highlight sentences about money, deadlines and email addresses.
Some details are true but do not help you decide – for example, the amount of the scholarship.
Pair each detail in the email with the official rule it breaks.
interviews: Ask the Scholarship Office about fees and results.
Ask IT Support whether anyone has checked the email.
Ask Emma what she has already done.
analysis: Verified evidence comes from official documents or checks; claims by the sender are unverified.
Support your conclusion with evidence from both the email and official sources.
Avoid conclusions that no document can prove.
report: Follow the five sections: summary, evidence, analysis, conclusion, recommendations.
Use linking words such as 'however', 'in addition' and 'therefore'.
Give practical recommendations for Emma and for other students.

sampleSolution.report:
Summary: On 3 March 2027, Emma Tran received an email saying she had won a $5,000 scholarship. The sender asked her to pay a $150 processing fee within 48 hours and to send her passport and bank card number.

Evidence collected: The official announcement says the university never asks students to pay any fee and that official emails end in @iu.edu. However, the email came from awards@intl-univ-scholarships.com. The IT report shows that this domain was registered on 1 March, only two days before the email. In addition, results are published on the Student Portal on 20 March, not by private email.

Analysis: The email copies real details, such as the amount and Mr. Miller's name, but it breaks several official rules.

Conclusion: The email is a phishing scam.

Recommendations: Emma should not pay or send any personal data. She should forward the email to security@iu.edu. The university should also warn all students about this scam.
